full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff filed the present Admiralty Suit against the defendants for recovery of its claim for a sum of USS 5,17,000 equivalent to Taka 4,01,96,750 from the defendants as damages and compensation for loss and damage suffered by the plaintiff resulting from collision between the plaintiff's vessel Ruby Star with the defendant No. 1 vessel MV Athens (formerly MV Hansa) IMO No. 8913667 occurred on 25-10-2013, now lying in the Jahanarabad Yard, Kadamrasul, Sitakunda, Chittagong. Upon an application filed by the plaintiff for arrest of the vessel MV Athens (ex MV Hansa) this court ordered for arrest of the said vessel on 24-11-2013. 

 3. Defendant No. 9 Arefin Enterprise, appeared in the suit on 13-1-2014 and filed the present application for vacating the order of arrest of the vessel MV Athens stating that this defendant opened Letter of Credit No. 1472-1302-0045 dated 7-11-2013 for importing the vessel namely MV Athens for scrapping the same as per Memorandum of Agreement dated 2-11-2013; that thereafter the defendant-applicant submitted Bill of Entry No. C-1407000 dated 10-11-2013 before the Customs Authority for releasing the same and after completion of all legal formalities got release order from Custom Authority started scrapping the vessel and as such it ceased to be vessel and lost its legal character to navigate; that the aforesaid vessel has been delisted from the shipping registry and the Government of Bangladesh has given all necessary permissions to beach and cut the same and when the vessel was beached it had lost its power to navigate on water and hence cannot be treated as a ship under the definition of a 'ship' as per section 2(b) of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000; that the plaintiff in its plaint clearly admitted that the plaintiff's claim in the present suit is for recovery of the alleged damages done by the defendant No. 1 vessel MV Athens on 25-10-2013 outside the territorial jurisdiction of Bangladesh and the defendants No. 3, 4 and 5 were the former owners on the date of occurrence of collision and the defendant No. 9 is the current owner of defendant No. 1 MV Athens and the vessel was purchased for the purpose of scrapping and at present lying at the beaching yard at Jahanarabad Yard, Kadam Rasul, Sitakunda, Chittagong. It was further stated that the said vessel arrived at Chittagong Port on 14-11-2013 and the said vessel was ready for scrapping on 16-11-2014. Thus it is apparent that at the date of filing of the present suit on 24-11-2014 the defendant Nos. 3, 4 and 5 are the previous owners of the defendant No. 1 vessel had no beneficial interest in the defendant No. 1 vessel and as such the suit is not maintainable within the jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court. It was also stated that since the applicant has already started scrapping the vessel and as such the said vessel has become scrapped goods which lost the legal character to navigate either mechanically or legally as such the order of arrest cannot be sustained in the eye of law. It was also alleged that on the date of filing of the present suit and the order of arrest was made, the defendant No. 1 vessel was not a ship in the eye of law against which an action in rem could be initiated. With these averments, the plaintiff prayed for vacating the order of arrest on the ground of lack of jurisdiction and not maintainable in the eye of law and the order of arrest is liable to be vacated. 

 4. Against the application for vacating the order of arrest, plaintiff-opposite-party filed written objection dated 22-1-2014 stating, inter-alia, that the statement made in paragraph Nos. 5, 7 and 10 of the vessel are incorrect and not based on record. It appears from the documents filed by the defendant-applicant that the applicant did not obtain necessary permission for cutting the vessel on 10-11-2013 and 16-11-2013 when the vessel was released from the Customs Authority and all the aforesaid statements made with a view to mislead the court in order to avoid liability and the jurisdiction of the Hon'ble Court. The vessel MV Athens did not lose the nature and legal characteristic of a 'ship' as defined in section 2(b) of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000 when the order of arrest of the vessel was passed on 24-11-2013 or served on 25-11-2013. From the documents filed by the applicant, it transpires that defendant No. 9 did not obtain necessary permission for scrapping of the vessel MV Athens when the order of arrest of the vessel was passed on 24-11-2013. The said vessel was still afloat near the mouth of the beaching yard and had not been beached or scrapped on 25-11-2013, when service of the order of arrest was effected by the Marshall of this court on the vessel MV Athens. During the service, a staff of the plaintiff's counsel was also present and at the time of service the order of arrest by the Marshall, the vessel was afloat. It also appears that when the order of arrest was passed, necessary permissions for the scrapping of the vessel were not obtained as per the Ship Breaking and Recycling Rules, 2011. Particularly, the defendant No. 9 failed to produce the necessary environment clearance certificate from the Department of Environment and Treasury Challan in favour of the Ship Building and Ship Recycling Board ("SBSRB"), certificate from the Department of Explosives, Ship Recycling Plan (SRP) approved by the SBSRB and necessary cutting permission from the SBSRB which are all required before scrapping process can be started. The statement that the vessel MV Athens ceased to be a 'ship' as defined under section 2(b) of the Act, 2000 as soon as the ship entered the territorial water of Bangladesh, beached and lost its power to navigate on water is clearly misstatement of fact aimed at misleading this Hon'ble Court. It is a settled principle of law that the Admiralty Court has jurisdiction over any claim for damage done by any ship without any distinction as to whether the ship is a sea going ship or an inland ship. The expression 'ship' as defined in section 2(kha) of the Ain that is “জাহাজ” অর্থ নৌ পরিবহনে ব্যবহৃত হয় এমন যে কোন জলযান (vessel) অন্তর্ভূক্ত হইবে। In addition the Ship Breaking and Recycling Rules, 2011 in Rule 2 clearly defines a 'ship' means vessels and floating structures of any type operated in the marine environment and shall include submersibles, floating crafts, floating platforms, self-elevating platforms, floating Storage Unit, floating production storage units and offloading units, a vessel stripped of equipment or being towed destined for breaking purpose. Till 25-11-2013 the vessel was in a navigable condition as it was afloat near the beaching yard after being taken there by navigation. Since the necessary permissions for the scrapping of the vessel were not in place at the time of arrest of the vessel and the vessel was afloat at the time of the order of arrest, the vessel MV Athens did not cease to be a 'ship' within the meaning of law. 

 6. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, Senior Advocate with Mr Omar Sadat, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant No. 9 firstly, submits that the plaintiff suit in action in rem is not entertainable within the jurisdiction of this court for non-fulfillment of the requirement of the provisions of section 4 (4) (ka) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 (shortly, the Ain) as would be apparent from the provisions of law and the facts stated as admitted in the plaint of the present suit. 

 7. Secondly, he submits that the plaintiff has also brought the present Admiralty Suit in action in personam against the owners of the defendant No. 1 vessel disclosing the cause of action as arising out of a collision between the plaintiff's vessel RUBY STAR with the defendant No. 1 vessel MV Athens occurred in Hong Kong on 25-10-2013 beyond the territorial waters of Bangladesh as such the plaintiff suit in action in personam is not entertainable and maintainable within the jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court for non-fulfillment of the provisions of section 5(1) (kha) and 5(5) of the said Ain. 

 8. He finally submits that the defendant No. 1 vessel MV Athens having had ceased to be a ship before the issuance and the service of order of arrest on 24-11-2013 within the meaning of ship as defined in section 2(kha) of the said Ain, the plaintiffs suit in action in rem against the defendant No. 1 vessel is not entertainable and amenable within the jurisdiction of this court under sections 2, 3 and 4 of the said Ain. In this connection Mr Alam has referred the case of Poplen Shipping Company Ltd. vs Commercial Union Assurance Company Ltd. (1943) 1 KB 161, Steed Man vs Scofield (1992) Lloyd's Law Reports, Vol-2163. 

 9. On the other hand, Dr Sharif Bhuiyan, with Mr Moin Ghani, and Mr Tanim Hussain Shawon, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party. Dr. Sharif Bhuiyan, learned Advocate submits that the plaintiff invoked the Admiralty Jurisdiction of the Hon'ble High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh under sub-section (3) of section 4 of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000 in action in rem to enforce a maritime lien arising from the damages caused by the defendant No. 1-vessel MV Athens during a collision with the plaintiff's vessel Ruby Star on 25-10-2013. 

 15. He finally submits that the maritime lien could not have elapsed due to latches. In the present the cause of action arose on 25-10-2013 in Hong Kong and the plaintiff instituted the present suit on 25-11-2013 and on the same day order of arrest was issued, which clearly shows that there was no latches as submitted by the learned Advocate for the defendants. In support of his submissions he referred to the decisions reported in 20 BLD (AD) 230 = 5 BLC (AD) 169, 34 DLR (AD) 110. He also relied British Shipping Laws, Volume 14 the Book Maritime Liens by Dr. Thomas. 

 16. The prime question to be decided in this suit as raised by the learned Advocate for both the parties that whether the plaintiff has a maritime lien over the defendant No. 1 vessel arising out of the damage caused during the collusion between the vessel Ruby Star and MV Athens in Hong Kong and whether the plaintiff is entitled to invoked the Admiralty Jurisdiction of this court to enforce action in rem to enforce maritime lien under section 4(3) of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 arising from damages caused by the MV Athens formerly MV Hansa during a collision with the plaintiff's vessel Ruby Star on 25-10-2013 in Hong Kong. 

 17. It appears that the plaintiff filed the present suit on 24-11-2013 impleading the present applicant as defendant No. 9 including MV Athens and others as principal defendant Nos. 1-8. It further appears that the plaintiff invoked jurisdiction of this court under sub-section (3) of section 4 the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 which reads as under:— 

 19. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, learned Senior Advocate for the defendant No. 9 submits that MV Athens is not 'ship' as defined in section 2(kha) of the Ain and section 2(47) of the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1983, since the vessel has been beached in the beaching yard for scrapping, the vessel will cease to have its mechanised navigability and as such will cease to be a 'ship' to be used in navigation within the ambit of clause (kha) of section 2 of the Ain. In support of this submission Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, learned Senior Advocate cited the case of Polen Shipping Company Limited vs Commercial Union Assurance Company Limited, 1 KB (1942) 161. The facts and circumstances of the case reported in 1 KB (1942) 161 are however, quite different. In the cited case the question before a learned Single Judge of the Kings Bench was whether a floating boat was a ship or vessel within the meaning of insurance policy under which the plaintiff was claiming on account of collision between the vessel and the above floating boat. It was held that a ship or a vessel is a hollow structure intended to be used in navigation, that is, to do its real work on the seas or other waters and capable of free and ordered movement thereon from one place to another. It was further held that floating boat did not fit in within the definition of ship and vessel and, therefore, there was no collision between the two vessels in terms of the insurance policy. 

 20. It may be pointed out that the arrest of a ship in an action in rem under Admiralty Jurisdiction is not an interlocutory order, the very jurisdiction of the Admiralty court is founded on the arrest of the vessel this is the essence of the procedure of action in rem. The arrest of the defendant vessel, on the filing the plaint and the application for arrest is the assumption of jurisdiction by court. The jurisdiction is founded on the presence of the vessel in the territorial waters of Bangladesh and the arrest of the vessel to answer to the claim of the plaintiff and providing security for such claim. 

 23. In the present case, as the vessel was already beached in the beaching yard at the time of filing of the above suit, the contention of Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, learned counsel for the defendants, that the vessel ceased to be navigable within the purview of clause (kha) of section 2 of the Ain, is not devoid of force. However, this does not necessarily lead to the conclusion that the above suit under the admiralty jurisdiction in terms of the Ain are not competent, if the plaintiffs had maritime lien over the vessel, the above suits are competent. 

 24. It appears that the plaintiff in their plaint averred that on the filing of the suit and on the date of service of notice of arrest upon the defendant vessel was afloat in the Jahanabad beaching yard. Thus the submission made by the learned Senior Advocate Mr Kamal-ul-Alam within the purview of clause (kha) of section 2 of the Ain is not devoid of force. 

 25. The next question to be considered is that whether the plaintiff is entitled to invoke the Admiralty Jurisdiction under sub-section (3) of section 4 of the Admiralty Ain, 2000 in an action in rem to enforce maritime lien. It is apparent from the plaint specially paragraph No. 5 of the plaint that the plaintiff has maritime lien over defendant No. 1 vessel arises during collision on 25-10-2013. In this regard we may refer to the provision of sub-section (3) and (4) of section 4 of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 which roads as follows: 

 32. It appears that the plaintiff filed the present suit invoking the Admiralty Jurisdiction of this court under section 4(3) of the Ain in an action in rem to enforce maritime lien. A suit in rem does not change its nature and character because the owners and parties interested in have been identified and impleaded in the plaint. In the present suit the ship (res) has been impleaded as defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2 has been described as "owners and parties interested in" the vessel of defendant No. 1 and the defendant No. 9 as current owner was impleaded in the suit. The fact that the current owners of the ship, defendant No. 9 have been impleaded and identified in the suit does not mean that suit ceases to be action in rem. 

 34. It further appears that the plaintiff does not invoke the jurisdiction of this court in personam under section 5 of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000. Therefore, there is no need to establish that the cause of action arose in the internal or territorial waters of Bangladesh. The action is not action in personam and which is clear from the plaint that the plaintiff have not sought an arrest or attachment of the property of the defendants owners but only sought an arrest of the ship (res) -defendant No. 1 in a suit arising from an action in rem to enforce a maritime lien on the arrested vessel, MV Athens (ex MV Hansa). 

 35. It cannot be denied that the Admiralty Court in Bangladesh prior to the enforcement of the Admiralty Court Ain, 2000 (Act XLIII of 2000) were exercising admiralty jurisdiction in order to enforce the maritime lien and, therefore, by virtue of the above proviso, the above jurisdiction remained intact apart from the express jurisdiction conferred on the High Court under the Ain by sub-section (3) of section 4 which provides that admiralty jurisdiction can be exercised in any case, in which, there is a maritime lien. Thus the plaintiff's claim arising from maritime lien against the defendant vessel prima-facie fall under section 4(3) of the said Ain.
